components.css: .ds-reviews { background: #eef2f3; padding: 1.5rem 0; overflow: hidden; font-family: Archivo, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; color: #38494d; } .ds-track { display: flex; gap: 1.5rem; width: max-content; animation: ds-drift 30s linear infinite; } .ds-reviews:hover .ds-track, .ds-reviews:focus-within .ds-track { animation-play-state: paused; } @keyframes ds-drift { to { transform: translateX(calc(-50% - 0.75rem)); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-track { animation: none; } .ds-reviews { overflow-x: auto; } .ds-review[aria-hidden] { display: none; } } .ds-review { flex: none; width: 22rem; margin: 0; padding: 1.5rem; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #d5dde0; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-review blockquote { margin: 0; } .ds-review p { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; } .ds-review figcaption { margin-top: 0.875rem; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 700; font-stretch: 105%; }

components.css: .ds-slate-hero { background: #38494d; padding: 2rem 2rem 2.5rem 2.5rem; } .ds-hero-fig { position: relative; isolation: isolate; margin: 0; width: 14rem; } .ds-hero-fig::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; border-radius: 6px; background: #f9ff00; transform: translate(-18px, 18px); } .ds-hero-photo { aspect-ratio: 3 / 4; border-radius: 6px; background: linear-gradient(160deg, #7c8b8f, #2c3a3d); box-shadow: 0 30px 60px -30px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-hero-fig::before { animation: ds-panel-out 1s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) 0.3s both; } .ds-hero-photo { animation: ds-photo-rise 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; } @keyframes ds-panel-out { from { transform: none; } } @keyframes ds-photo-rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(1rem); } } }

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Tradesman's Own Page"**

A local tradesman's page done with care. The layout is the conventional one a homeowner expects from a plumber, and the identity comes entirely from the brand colours, one heavy extended grotesque, and the owners' own words. Nothing is themed, illustrated, or decorated; the craft is in proportion, rule weight, and the restraint of the yellow.

The page alternates white reading ground with slate bands (header, hero, footer) and one cool grey band for reviews. Content sits in a single 72rem column with generous section padding. Structure comes from fine horizontal rules and type scale, not from boxes; the reviews row is the one place quotes sit in cards. The only filled shape a visitor is asked to act on is the yellow call button, and it repeats wherever a decision might happen: header, hero, footer.

The system rejects the stock trades template: icon-card grids, hero stat counters, stock photography, and invented badges.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, slate bands, one cool grey band; yellow reserved for calling, plus the one panel behind the hero photo.
One family (Archivo variable) carrying everything: extended heavy for headings, regular width for text.
Fine rules instead of cards, with the drifting reviews row as the single card component; flat surfaces.
Sticky slate header that keeps the number on screen at every width.
Real proof only: the client's photo, quoted reviews, the 5.0 rating.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Call Rule
rules.body: Signal Yellow fills only things that start a phone call or mark the number, plus the map pin centre. The single decorative exception is the offset panel behind the hero photo (chosen by the user in live mode, 2026-11-23); it is not repeated on any other image or surface. Yellow never colours text, headings, borders, section backgrounds, or any other decoration.

rules.name: The Blue Is For Links Rule
rules.body: Link Blue appears only as link text and the light-surface focus ring. On slate bands the focus ring switches to Signal Yellow and links use On-Slate colours.

rules.name: The White Reading Ground Rule
rules.body: Long reading happens on pure white or the cool band, never on slate; slate bands carry headings, leads, and the call.

rules.name: The Width Carries Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings are always extended (112% to 118%) and heavy (700 to 850) with negative tracking; body is never extended. Do not introduce a second typeface.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every phone number is set with tabular numerals and bold weight.

rules.name: The Rules Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Content groups are separated by a top rule (1px Fine Rule, or 2px Workshop Slate for service blocks) and whitespace. The only bordered container is the review card (white, 1px Fine Rule, no shadow); no other text sits in a box, and no container carries a shadow.

dos: Do keep the yellow call button visible in the header at every width, and repeat it at the hero and footer.
Do set every heading in Archivo at 112% width or wider, 700 to 850 weight, with negative tracking.
Do separate content with top rules (1px `rule`, or 2px `slate` for service blocks) and whitespace.
Do keep reading text on white or the cool band, at 1.125rem with line-height 1.6 and max 66ch.
Do switch the focus ring to Signal Yellow on slate bands and keep it Link Blue on light surfaces.
Do use only real material: the client's photo and quoted reviews.
donts: Don't use Signal Yellow for text, borders, section backgrounds, or decoration beyond the one hero photo panel.
Don't put text in bordered or shadowed cards outside the reviews row, or build icon-card grids.
Don't add hero stat counters, stock photography, invented badges, or accreditations.
Don't set Link Blue on slate or on any tint darker than the cool band.
Don't introduce a second typeface or extend body text.
